title: Zeros as a divisor and as failure of surjectivity
claim: Two representations linearize the same vanishing data in different categories: canonical factorization stores zeros and multiplicities in an entire-function divisor whose logarithmic derivative is a partial-fraction sum, whereas the orbit-sum cokernel stores zeros as support of annihilating Mellin distributions and multiplicities as derivative-supported generalized eigenvectors. The bridge identifies multiplicity as the invariant preserved when moving from factor order to Jordan-type structure.
historical_or_program_relation: The classical entire-function program constrains the divisor through global growth; the later noncommutative-spectral program recodes that divisor as a range defect, shifting the central proof burden from factorization and normalization to construction and analysis of an operator representation.
limits: The indexed evidence does not show that the cokernel representation is selfadjoint or that its spectral interpretation proves RH, and the canonical product alone supplies no operator. The relation is a shared encoding of zeros and multiplicity, not an equivalence of the two full programs.

title: Trace terms require matching local singularity geometry
claim: A trace-formula transfer is controlled by local geometric and analytic invariants, not by the mere appearance of a sum over zeros and a sum over orbits: graph-diagonal transversality produces fixed-point weights through a return-map determinant, while a different pole multiplicity in the secondary zeta machinery forces a separate analytic treatment despite the Weil-Selberg analogy.
historical_or_program_relation: The sources connect the spectral-trace aspiration to a concrete obstruction audit: Connes derives contributions from flow geometry, while the secondary-zeta program explicitly rejects a literal import from the Selberg setting when the singularity structure does not match.
limits: Neither unit constructs a common dynamical system for the Riemann zeros, and matching one trace coefficient would not establish equivalence of trace formulas. The double-pole obstruction is specific to the cited secondary-zeta comparison.

title: Test functions turn prime-zero duality into a resolution budget
claim: Residue calculus exposes a bounded-height zero sum in prime-counting fluctuations, and admissible Fourier pairs or extremal trigonometric brackets make the resolution explicit: low frequencies can be transferred to prime-power terms, while truncation or unresolved high modes remain as an auditable error channel. Sharper localization therefore consumes more spectral bandwidth rather than arriving for free.
historical_or_program_relation: The classical truncated Perron contour and the Weil test-function formulation are refined by bandlimited majorant-minorant methods that separate interval-resolution error, arithmetically resolved modes, and the uncontrolled Fourier tail.
limits: These bridges do not assign an individual prime fluctuation to an individual zero, and the larger-bandwidth conclusion in the indexed source needs an additional hypothesis to control the tail. The relation is not an unconditional equivalence between arbitrary prime and zero statistics.

title: Zero-free width is a reusable but scale-dependent analytic currency
claim: Writing a zero-free region as a height-dependent boundary width exposes the quantity that contour displacement spends to suppress prime-counting errors. Once proved, a better width or constant can propagate through existing explicit-formula arguments to several prime-counting bounds, but asymptotically superior boundary geometry need not give the strongest finite-height consequence.
historical_or_program_relation: The qualitative route from zero exclusion to a quantitative prime number theorem becomes an explicit constant-propagation program, and later comparisons distinguish all-height certificates from asymptotically optimized Korobov-Vinogradov geometry.
limits: The indexed relations reuse cited downstream arguments rather than rederive every threshold and constant. Boundary forms that are asymptotically equivalent may still differ at finite heights, so no global ordering of regions is claimed.

title: Positive auxiliary functions coordinate many views of one hypothetical zero
claim: Zero-free proofs repeatedly replace separate shifted logarithmic-derivative estimates by one sign-controlled aggregate. Euler-product positivity couples harmonics, a nonnegative trigonometric polynomial aligns several heights so only the candidate zero retains its singular distance, and admissible smoothing kernels reduce the result to a finite scalar certificate whose parameters can be optimized.
historical_or_program_relation: The mechanism develops from fixed low-harmonic positivity to higher-degree polynomial and kernel design: the analytic architecture stays recognizable while the finite auxiliary object becomes an explicit constant-bearing proof interface.
limits: A numerically good coefficient vector or objective value is not a proof until global nonnegativity, correction signs, monotonicity, endpoint bounds, and rounding margins are certified. Aggregation deliberately loses termwise information and does not establish optimality over all auxiliary families.

title: Finite RH verification composes detection, certified signs, and completeness
claim: A finite critical-line verification is valid only when three layers compose: Riemann-Siegel compression supplies tractable real evaluations, error enclosures turn selected values into certified signs with adaptive refinement for exceptions, and an independent all-zero accounting theorem stitches computed ranges into a complete multiplicity-aware prefix. Finding apparent roots is therefore not the same operation as proving none were missed.
historical_or_program_relation: The computational program progresses from short real oscillatory evaluations and Gram-point screening to distributed range certificates with conservative numerical error, explicit provenance, boundary overrun, and a theorem-mediated completeness conclusion.
limits: The result remains bounded by its stated height or zero index and depends on the imported counting theorem and any preserved exception review. Certified signs alone neither prove simplicity nor certify the full zero count, and scale without reproducible provenance is not an independent correctness argument.

title: Universal local statistics and arithmetic lower-order structure coexist
claim: GUE agreement describes a normalized local universality class, while finite-height deviations and the hybrid Euler-Hadamard moment picture retain information that the universal leading law discards. The joint mechanism separates zero-statistical organization from prime-dependent arithmetic factors and structured lower-order terms instead of treating them as rival explanations.
historical_or_program_relation: The pair-correlation comparison motivates a random-matrix model; later finite-scale and moment analyses refine that model by assigning universal statistics to the zero side and arithmetic weights to Euler data.
limits: Agreement of local or limiting statistics does not identify zeta zeros with matrix eigenvalues pointwise or prove RH. The hybrid asymptotic and its lower-order polynomial are conjectural in the indexed evidence, and a finite-height deviation does not by itself diagnose its arithmetic cause.

title: A normalized close gap becomes a conditioned derivative-root problem
claim: Normalizing a zero gap by the local mean spacing makes rare close pairs comparable across heights; in the CUE derivative model, such a local collision is the input controlling a nearby derivative root, and conditioning on a double eigenvalue is converted into an ordinary lower-dimensional Haar ensemble reweighted by a fourth characteristic-polynomial moment. The bridge turns singular local geometry into a tractable change of measure.
historical_or_program_relation: Finite zeta computations expose exceptionally small normalized gaps, while the random-polynomial program supplies a mechanism for studying how collision geometry propagates to critical points through a conditioned ensemble.
limits: The observed zeta gap is a finite example, not a spacing law, and the collision-to-derivative mechanism is established for the CUE model rather than transferred as a theorem about zeta or zeta-prime. Shared normalization does not prove ensemble identity.

title: Spectral statistics diagnose candidates but do not supply the missing operator
claim: A credible Hilbert-Polya route must satisfy more than spectral reality or a statistical match: the candidate representation must reproduce trace coefficients, signs, multiplicities, and a valid operator domain. Density-form discordances constrain literal chaotic realizations, while a difference-conjugated non-Hermitian proposal still requires domain, metric, completeness, and reality arguments beyond its formal zero boundary condition.
historical_or_program_relation: The program moves from random-matrix naturality as a search diagnostic to explicit falsification criteria for trace-formula models and then to operator proposals whose unresolved analytic domains make the remaining burden visible.
limits: The indexed sources do not prove that any candidate operator realizes all nontrivial zeros or implies RH. PT invariance alone allows conjugate pairs, and disagreement with one literal trace model does not rule out every spectral construction.

title: Abundance, simplicity, and horizontal displacement are distinct zero observables
claim: Zero-distribution claims require multiple noninterchangeable summaries: a total count measures abundance, a simple-critical-line count refines both location and multiplicity, and a centered first moment of derivative-zero real parts measures signed horizontal bias. A signed moment can be small through cancellation even when many zeros lie far from the center, while a large line proportion says nothing by itself about derivative-zero displacement.
historical_or_program_relation: Positive-proportion work refines the RH question by counting critical-line and simple zeros; later derivative studies add weighted horizontal moments and compare them across derivative order, exposing a different residual geometry.
limits: None of these statistics determines the full point process. The derivative-zero moment is not a statistic of the original zeta zeros, OCR obscures some exact coefficients in its source, and RH-conditional one-sided interpretations must not be read into the unconditional signed sum.

title: Mollification changes the detector and creates coupled proof obligations
claim: When raw moment inequalities are poorly aligned with a desired zero or nonvanishing population, a mollifier redesigns the observable so Littlewood-type geometry becomes an evaluable mean square. Expanding a multi-piece mollifier then reveals that admissibility is joint: diagonal estimates are insufficient because cross terms impose their own length and mean-value constraints.
historical_or_program_relation: The mollified critical-line proportion method turns geometric zero information into an optimized energy, while later family and multi-piece analyses clarify why detector design and the interaction graph—not merely sharper unweighted moments or longer individual pieces—govern the attainable proportion.
limits: The cited applications concern different zeta and L-function populations and do not share one numerical constant or theorem. Mollification does not itself provide cancellation; every diagonal and cross mean value, parameter range, and imported hypothesis remains a separate proof burden.

title: Zero density is routed through regime-sensitive large-value control
claim: A zero-density problem can be rerouted to counts of large Dirichlet-polynomial values and then constrained by critical-line moments or pointwise inputs. Moment order tunes sensitivity to the upper tail, prime-sum majorants expose a tractable surrogate, and complementary large-value estimates dominate in different parameter regions; the correct object is therefore a phase diagram of estimators rather than one globally best bound.
historical_or_program_relation: Moment methods supply an average-to-tail interface, while newer simultaneous-large-value and contour-transfer arguments make correlations and replaceable estimator modules visible before propagating the bound back to zero density.
limits: The indexed large-value source describes part of the reduction strategically and leaves some quantitative factors outside the readable span. Moment control does not localize individual zeros, and replacing an estimator still requires its own range, length, and averaging hypotheses.

title: Subtracting smooth counts exposes argument variation as the live channel
claim: Across absolute, relative, and derivative-zero counting, contour formulas separate a smooth main count from boundary argument variation. Subtracting two L-function counts cancels shared deterministic growth and turns argument differences into relative rank excursions; for derivative zeros, the analogous subtraction leaves an additional arg G_k channel that controls the precision after the main terms are settled.
historical_or_program_relation: Backlund-style all-zero accounting uses theta plus S(T); relative-zero work exploits cancellation between two such counting formulas; higher-derivative work shows that changing the analytic object preserves the contour architecture but introduces a new phase bottleneck.
limits: The relative-count bridge is only controlled up to source-dependent errors and endpoint conventions, and the derivative formulas require RH for their sharpened form. Argument variation is an intermediate statistic, not itself a zero locator, and the indexed derivative source reports an uncontrolled constant.

title: Zero locations supply possible modes, but observables choose their amplitudes
claim: Canonical product theory treats the zero divisor as global analytic data, while reverse Mellin mapping turns those zero locations into candidate exponents in a geometric averaging error. The coefficient of each exponent is nevertheless an observable-dependent spectral projection, and orthogonality can force every such residue to vanish for a particular theta observable without removing the underlying zeros.
historical_or_program_relation: The classical divisor-centered description is carried into a modular-spectral setting where zeros parameterize possible horocycle error modes; the later representation refines the bridge by separating universal pole locations from observable coupling amplitudes.
limits: The indexed horocycle expansion leaves termwise control of the zero sum unproved, and vanishing residues for one observable do not imply RH, zero absence, or vanishing for other observables. The canonical product does not itself supply the modular projection coefficients.

title: Bounded verification can feed theorems but cannot settle asymptotic behavior
claim: Finite computation has two legitimate but sharply bounded roles: it can certify the hypothesis of another theorem up to a parameterized height, and it can reveal local anomalies that guide search. It cannot distinguish global boundedness from extremely slow divergence by appearance alone, nor can qualitative deterioration in a finite run overturn a simultaneously certified critical-line prefix.
historical_or_program_relation: The computational RH tradition evolves from reporting ever larger verified prefixes to treating the cutoff as an interface lemma consumed by conditional consequences, alongside an explicit methodological warning against visual or finite-range extrapolation.
limits: No finite cutoff proves RH or any unbounded asymptotic, and the addendum's word 'worse' is undefined in the indexed evidence. Downstream consequences inherit the exact hypotheses and range of the external theorem that consumes the finite certificate.
